items.title: City Council Approves Bike-Share Expansion
items.text: The city council voted 7 to 4 on Tuesday to expand its bike-share program to six more neighborhoods by next spring. Supporters argue that the plan will reduce traffic and give residents a cheap alternative to buses, which have become more crowded in recent years. Opponents, however, question whether the budget of 4.2 million dollars is justified, pointing out that only one in eight residents used the service last year. "We should fix the roads first," said Councilor Han Mirae, who voted against the plan. A transport official responded that use rose sharply wherever stations were placed near schools and train stops, and that the new stations will follow the same pattern. A final cost report is due in January, and the council has promised to publish it online.

qs.q: What is the article mainly about?
o: A new traffic law that requires all cyclists to wear safety helmets
A survey showing that most residents now prefer cycling to buses
A vote to widen a bike-share service despite objections
A budget crisis that has forced the city to close several bus lines
qs.why: 기사의 중심은 시의회가 반대 의견에도 자전거 공유 서비스를 확대하기로 했다는 것이에요.

qs.q: According to the article, why do opponents doubt the plan?
o: Few residents used the service last year, so the cost seems too high
Cyclists have caused many accidents on the roads near the new stations
The council voted without listening to the views of local schools
Buses have become cheaper and less crowded than they used to be
qs.why: 반대자들은 작년 이용률이 낮은 점을 들어 예산에 의문을 제기했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the new stations?
o: They will be placed mainly in areas where very few people live
They will replace the stations that already exist downtown
They will be free for everyone during the first year of use
They will probably be built close to schools and train stops
qs.why: 교통 담당자가 같은 방식(학교·기차역 근처)을 따를 것이라고 했으므로 그렇게 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: The word "justified" in the passage is closest in meaning to
o: reduced
reasonable
postponed
advertised
qs.why: budget is justified는 '예산이 타당하다'는 뜻이므로 reasonable이 가장 가까워요.

qs.q: Why is the final cost report mentioned at the end?
o: To explain why the final vote was delayed until the following spring
To show that the public will be able to check the spending later
To prove that the new stations have already been completed
To warn readers that the program may be cancelled in January
qs.why: 보고서를 온라인에 공개하겠다는 말은 지출을 나중에 확인할 수 있다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Introducing the PulseBand 5
items.text: Meet the PulseBand 5, the smartwatch that "understands your body better than you do." With a battery that lasts up to nine days*, an always-on display and sleep tracking trusted by thousands of users, it is the only wearable you will ever need. Customers tell us they feel "healthier within a week," and our designers have spent three years making every detail perfect. Order before Friday and receive a free charging stand worth $39. Don't wait: only 500 units remain at this price! Join the thousands who have already made the switch. *Based on typical use with the display set to auto-dim and all notifications switched off. Battery life varies depending on settings and conditions.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the text?
o: To warn buyers about faults found in a wearable device
To compare several smartwatches by price and quality
To report the results of a study on sleep and health
To persuade readers to buy a product soon
qs.why: 광고문으로, 독자가 빨리 제품을 구매하도록 설득하는 것이 목적이에요.

qs.q: Why does the writer say "only 500 units remain at this price"?
o: To create pressure so that readers decide quickly
To explain why the watch is difficult to manufacture
To apologize for a shortage of charging stands in stores
To show that the price has risen since last month
qs.why: 한정 수량을 강조해 서둘러 결정하게 하는 설득 기법이에요.

qs.q: What does the note marked with an asterisk suggest about the nine-day battery claim?
o: The figure was measured on an older model of the watch
The figure is lower than the figure for rival watches
The figure is true only under particular settings
The figure applies only to people who sleep nine hours
qs.why: 별표 문구는 특정 설정에서만 9일이 가능하다고 조건을 달고 있어요.

qs.q: Which statement is a careful reader MOST justified in making?
o: The nine-day battery life is guaranteed for every owner
The free stand will be offered to anyone who orders later
Thousands of users have reported measurable health gains
The claim that it understands the body is promotional, not proven
qs.why: '몸을 이해한다'는 말은 증명되지 않은 홍보 표현이에요. 나머지는 본문에서 보장되거나 언급된 적이 없어요.

items.title: A Week Without Plastic Bottles
items.text: Post by @greenlife_jun: "Just finished a week without buying a single plastic bottle. I carried a refillable one everywhere, and my wallet is already happier! #zerowaste" Reply by @daily_dan: "Nice, but didn't you fly to a conference last month? Seems a bit hypocritical to me." Reply by @greenlife_jun: "Fair point, Dan. I can't undo that trip, but I'd rather do something than nothing. I'm trying to change the habits I can control, one at a time." Reply by @ecomeg: "Please stop attacking people who are at least trying. Small steps add up, and posts like this are how I learned to start. Thanks for the tips, Jun, and keep sharing your progress with us!"

qs.q: How would you describe the tone of @daily_dan's reply?
o: Warm and encouraging
Doubtful and slightly critical
Confused, apologetic and anxious
Playful and humorous
qs.why: 댄은 칭찬 뒤에 비꼬는 듯 위선이라고 지적해 비판적이에요.

qs.q: What attitude does @greenlife_jun show toward the criticism?
o: Anger that leads to deleting the original post
Denial that the conference trip ever took place
Calm acceptance without giving up the effort
Disinterest in what other users think of the habit
qs.why: 준은 '맞는 지적'이라고 인정하면서도 노력을 계속하겠다고 해요.

qs.q: In the second reply, "the habits I can control" most likely refers to
o: everyday choices such as what to buy and carry
decisions that the government makes about recycling
trips that other people take for work
the number of followers who read the post
qs.why: 자신이 통제할 수 있는 습관은 일상의 선택(구매·휴대품)을 가리켜요.

qs.q: Why did @ecomeg write a reply?
o: To defend @greenlife_jun and support small efforts
To correct a factual error in the original post
To advertise a different reusable product
To ask @greenlife_jun for money to support a campaign
qs.why: 메그는 노력하는 사람을 공격하지 말라며 준을 옹호해요.

items.title: Statement from Brightway Transit
items.text: Brightway Transit today announced that its night bus routes will run every fifteen minutes instead of every thirty, starting on the first of November. The change follows a three-month trial in which late-evening ridership grew by almost a quarter. "Our riders told us that waiting in the dark was the main reason they chose other ways to get home," said operations manager Lena Ortiz. The company stressed that fares will not change and that the new schedule will be reviewed after six months. Brightway also said it will hire forty additional drivers, although it declined to say how the expansion will be paid for. Questions from the media may be sent to the press office by email.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of this statement?
o: To defend the company against a complaint by drivers
To ask riders to vote on a new fare system
To inform the public and the media about a service change
To explain why the night routes will be shut down
qs.why: 보도자료로, 야간 버스 운행 간격 변경을 알리는 것이 목적이에요.

qs.q: Which detail does the statement leave unanswered?
o: When the new schedule will start
How the larger service will be financed
How long the trial lasted
Whether ticket prices will change for night riders
qs.why: 회사는 확장 비용을 어떻게 마련할지 밝히기를 거부했어요.

qs.q: The phrase "declined to say" suggests that the company
o: was unable to find the answer
forgot to include the details
had not yet decided what to do about it
chose not to give that information
qs.why: decline은 '정중히 거절하다'라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why does the statement quote operations manager Lena Ortiz?
o: To prove that the trial was run by an independent group
To give a reason for the change in the words of someone involved
To criticize riders who stopped using night buses
To announce that she will leave the company soon
qs.why: 담당자의 말을 인용해 변경의 이유를 뒷받침해요.

qs.q: Which of the following is stated in the text?
o: Late-evening ridership increased during the trial.
The fares for night buses will fall next month.
Every route in the city will run twice as often.
The review of the schedule will take place next week.
qs.why: 시범 기간 동안 늦은 저녁 이용객이 약 25퍼센트 늘었다고 해요. 나머지는 사실과 달라요.

items.title: Correction: School Lunch Figures
items.text: In our report "Lunch Lines Grow at Eastfield High," published on Monday, we stated that 40 percent of students now buy school lunch. The correct figure is 14 percent. The error arose because our reporter misread a table from the school district, in which 40 percent referred to the share of students who are eligible for lunch support, not the share who buy lunch. The headline and the third paragraph have been changed online. We also incorrectly named the cafeteria manager as Mr. Okafor; her name is Ms. Okafor. We apologize to the students, staff and readers affected by these mistakes. Readers who find an error in our reporting can contact the standards editor directly.

qs.q: What is the purpose of this notice?
o: To announce a change in the school's lunch menu
To defend the reporter against unfair criticism
To invite readers to write their own news stories for the school paper
To fix mistakes in an earlier article and apologize for them
qs.why: 정정 보도로, 이전 기사의 오류를 바로잡고 사과해요.

qs.q: What caused the wrong percentage?
o: The school refused to give any numbers
A student gave false information on purpose
A table was misread by the reporter
The headline was written before the interview
qs.why: 표의 40퍼센트는 지원 대상 비율이었는데 기자가 잘못 읽었어요.

qs.q: What does the number 40 percent actually describe?
o: The students who bring lunch from home
The students who skip lunch every day
The students who can receive lunch support
The staff members who eat in the cafeteria
qs.why: 40퍼센트는 급식 지원 대상 학생의 비율이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the newspaper from this notice?
o: It rarely checks any figures before it publishes an article
It is willing to publicly admit and repair its errors
It has stopped covering school news
It blames the school district for every mistake
qs.why: 오류를 공개적으로 인정하고 수정했으므로 투명하게 바로잡는 태도를 알 수 있어요.

items.title: Search Results: Does Food Affect Mood?
items.text: A student searches for "foods that improve mood" and finds three results. Result one is a blog called HappyPlate, which promises that "seven miracle foods cure sadness overnight." Its author is unnamed, and the page is full of links to buy supplements. Result two comes from a university medical center. Titled "Diet and Mood: What the Research Shows," it was reviewed by two named doctors in March and lists twelve studies at the bottom. It says the evidence is promising but not yet conclusive. Result three is a forum thread where a user writes, "My cousin ate bananas daily and was cured." The student must decide which source to trust for a school presentation.

qs.q: Which result would be the best source for the presentation?
o: The university medical center page
The HappyPlate blog post
The forum thread about bananas
All three, since they cover the same topic
qs.why: 저자·검토자·참고 연구가 밝혀진 대학 의료 센터 자료가 가장 믿을 만해요.

qs.q: Why should the student be careful with result one?
o: Its title is too long to fit on one screen
It lists too many studies for readers to follow
It was reviewed by doctors who disagree with each other
Its author is unknown and it seems to be selling something
qs.why: 익명 저자와 보충제 판매 링크는 신뢰도를 떨어뜨리는 단서예요.

qs.q: What does the university page say about the evidence?
o: It proves that bananas can cure sadness
It shows that diet has no link with mood
It is too old to be used as a source for research
It looks hopeful but cannot yet prove the idea
qs.why: 증거가 유망하지만 아직 결정적이지는 않다고 해요.

qs.q: The word "conclusive" in the passage is closest in meaning to
o: settled beyond doubt
impossible to read aloud
recently updated
widely advertised
qs.why: conclusive는 '결정적인, 의심의 여지 없는'이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Which feature of result three weakens its value as evidence?
o: It was written on a forum
It rests on one personal story
It mentions a common fruit
It was posted by a relative
qs.why: 한 사람의 경험담(일화)은 근거로 약해요. 포럼에 올랐다는 사실 자체가 약점은 아니에요.

items.title: Are Short Videos Shrinking Our Attention?
items.text: Every evening, millions of teenagers scroll through short videos that last less than fifteen seconds. Critics claim that this habit is damaging our ability to concentrate, and many parents agree. However, the evidence is thinner than the headlines suggest. Most studies show only that heavy users of short videos also tend to struggle with long tasks; they do not show which came first. A student who is already bored by homework may simply reach for the phone more often. What is clear is that apps are designed to keep us watching, using endless scrolling and automatic replay. Rather than blaming the format, we should ask who benefits when we stop choosing what to watch and let a machine decide.

qs.q: What is the writer's main argument?
o: Short videos should be banned for everyone under the age of eighteen without exception
Parents are wrong to worry about how teenagers use phones
The link to weak attention is unproven, but app design deserves scrutiny
Long videos are always better for learning than short ones
qs.why: 인과가 입증되지 않았지만 앱 설계는 따져 봐야 한다는 것이 글쓴이의 주장이에요.

qs.q: What does the writer mean by "they do not show which came first"?
o: The studies were published before the apps were invented
The studies failed to ask teenagers about their age
The studies cannot tell whether videos cause weak focus or the reverse
The studies compared videos with books in the wrong order
qs.why: 원인과 결과의 순서를 알 수 없다는 뜻이에요(상관관계와 인과관계의 구분).

qs.q: What is the writer's attitude toward the headlines?
o: Doubtful about how strongly they state the case
Pleased with how clearly and fairly they explain it
Angry that they ignore the apps' makers
Unconcerned about what they say
qs.why: 증거가 헤드라인보다 빈약하다고 하므로 회의적이에요.

qs.q: Which feature of apps does the writer criticize?
o: Rules that limit how long each video can be
Settings that let parents control the daily screen time of teenagers
Filters that hide videos made by strangers
Features that make users keep watching without choosing
qs.why: 무한 스크롤과 자동 재생이 시청을 이어 가게 만든다고 비판해요.

qs.q: In the last sentence, "a machine" most likely refers to
o: a camera
a recommendation system
a school computer
a parent's phone
qs.why: 무엇을 볼지 대신 정해 주는 것은 추천 알고리즘이에요.

items.title: Fact Check: The Flooded Subway Photo
items.text: A dramatic photo of a subway station filled with brown water has been shared more than 80,000 times this week, with captions claiming it shows yesterday's storm in our city. Our team ran the image through a reverse image search and found the same picture in a news archive from 2019. It was taken in another country, after a pipe burst under a main road. Local transit officials confirmed that none of our stations flooded during yesterday's rain. The photo itself is real, but the claim attached to it is false. We contacted several accounts that shared it; two have deleted their posts, and one has added a note explaining the mistake. Rating: Misleading.

qs.q: Why is the claim rated "Misleading"?
o: The photo was created by a computer program
A real photo was presented as proof of an event it does not show
The photo showed a station that does not exist
The photo showed a storm that was much worse than the captions claimed
qs.why: 사진은 진짜지만 다른 시기·장소의 것이라 설명이 사실과 달라요.

qs.q: How did the team discover where the photo came from?
o: By asking the people who shared it
By measuring the water level in the picture with special software
By reading the comments under the captions
By running the image through a reverse image search
qs.why: 역이미지 검색으로 2019년 보도 자료에서 같은 사진을 찾았어요.

qs.q: What is the function of the statement from transit officials?
o: It supplies independent evidence against the claim
It proves that the photo was edited
It explains why the pipe burst in 2019
It confirms that the storm caused serious damage
qs.why: 관계자의 확인은 주장에 반하는 별도의 근거를 제공해요.

qs.q: What can be concluded from the last part of the text?
o: Every account that shared the photo apologized
The fact-checkers blocked all of the accounts that had shared it
Some people who shared the photo accepted that it was wrong
Most readers still believe the original captions
qs.why: 두 계정은 게시물을 지웠고 한 계정은 정정 글을 달았어요. 모두 사과한 것은 아니에요.

items.title: Review: The Quiet Lantern Headphones
items.text: Disclosure: the manufacturer sent me these headphones free of charge, though I was not paid to write a positive review. After two weeks of daily use, my verdict is mostly good. The sound is warm and the noise cancelling handles train rumble well, but it struggles with voices in a busy cafe. The ear cushions are comfortable for about three hours; after that, my ears feel hot. Battery life matched the company's claim of thirty hours, which impressed me. At $199, they cost less than some rivals, yet the plastic hinge feels fragile. If you commute and want comfort over a short trip, they are a sound choice. If you work in noisy offices, look elsewhere.

qs.q: Why does the reviewer begin with a disclosure?
o: So the company can pay for the review afterward
So readers know the reviewer dislikes the brand
So the headphones can be returned for a refund
So readers can judge whether the free product may affect the opinion
qs.why: 무료 제품을 받았다는 사실을 밝혀 독자가 편향 가능성을 판단하게 해요.

qs.q: Which statement best summarizes the review?
o: They are the best headphones in every situation
They suit short commutes but have limits in noise and long wear
They are too expensive to be worth buying at all
They are comfortable for a full workday in a noisy open office
qs.why: 장단점을 고루 다루며 통근에는 좋지만 시끄러운 곳과 장시간 착용엔 한계가 있다고 해요.

qs.q: The phrase "handles train rumble well" shows that the headphones
o: break down on crowded platforms
play music louder than trains
reduce low, steady noise effectively
make voices clearer in cafes
qs.why: 기차의 낮은 소음을 잘 차단한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What is the reviewer's attitude toward the battery?
o: Pleasantly surprised that the claim was accurate
Disappointed that it needs charging every few days
Suspicious of the company's measurements
Indifferent to how long it lasts
qs.why: 회사의 주장과 일치해서 인상적이라고 해요.

qs.q: Which point is NOT a criticism in the review?
o: The price compared with that of rivals
The comfort of the cushions after several hours
The strength of the hinge
The noise cancelling in cafes
qs.why: 가격은 경쟁 제품보다 싸다고 하므로 비판이 아니에요.

items.title: The Voice on the Phone
items.text: Last month, the finance manager of a small company received a call from what sounded exactly like her chief executive. The voice asked her to transfer 20,000 dollars to a new supplier at once, and to keep the matter confidential. She complied. Only later did she discover that the caller had used software to copy the executive's voice from a public interview. Experts warn that such "voice cloning" scams are spreading because only a few seconds of audio are needed. They advise organizations to agree on a secret code word, to call back on a known number before sending money, and to be suspicious of any request that combines urgency with secrecy. "A familiar voice is no longer proof of identity," said one researcher.

qs.q: What is the main point of the article?
o: Company executives should avoid giving public interviews or speeches
Finance managers are usually careless with money
Copied voices can trick people, so requests need to be verified
Phone calls are always safer than written messages
qs.why: 음성 복제 사기를 소개하고 요청을 확인하는 방법을 알려 줘요.

qs.q: Which warning sign do the experts mention?
o: A call that comes late in the evening
A demand that is both urgent and secret
A caller who speaks with an accent
A supplier with a long and respected company history
qs.why: 긴급함과 비밀 유지를 함께 요구하는 요청을 의심하라고 해요.

qs.q: The word "complied" is closest in meaning to
o: argued with the caller
reported the call at once
hesitated for a long time
did what she was asked
qs.why: comply는 '요구에 따르다'라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: How did the criminals most likely obtain the voice?
o: From a private phone call at the bank
From audio that was available publicly
From a recording stolen from the office
From a message sent by the real executive
qs.why: 공개된 인터뷰에서 음성을 복제했다고 나와요.

qs.q: What does the researcher's quotation suggest?
o: Hearing a known voice does not guarantee who is speaking
Voices are impossible to copy with software
Every familiar caller should be trusted
Identity can only be proven by a signature
qs.why: 익숙한 목소리가 신원을 증명하지 못한다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: What Happens to Your Data?
items.text: When you create an account with PicShare, we collect your name, email address and the photos you upload. We also record the type of device you use, your approximate location and how long you spend on each page. We use this information to run the service, to show you advertising that we think you may like, and to improve our features. We may share limited data with advertising partners; we do not sell your photos. You may delete your account at any time, but copies of some data may remain in our backups for up to ninety days. By continuing to use PicShare, you agree to these terms. To change your choices, open Settings and select Privacy.

qs.q: What is the main function of this text?
o: To advertise a new photo-editing feature
To teach users how to take better photographs
To warn users that their account will soon be closed for breaking the rules
To explain what information an app collects and how it is used
qs.why: 개인정보 처리 방침으로, 수집 정보와 사용 방식을 설명해요.

qs.q: According to the text, what might happen to data after an account is deleted?
o: All data is passed to advertising partners
Photos are sold to other companies
Some copies may be kept for a limited time
Nothing at all is stored anywhere
qs.why: 백업에 최대 90일간 일부 데이터가 남을 수 있다고 해요.

qs.q: Which of the following is collected by the app?
o: The user's bank password
The user's home address in full
How long a user stays on each page
The names of the user's friends at school
qs.why: 페이지별 체류 시간을 기록한다고 나와요.

qs.q: The sentence "By continuing to use PicShare, you agree to these terms" implies that
o: users must sign a paper before they can log in again
using the service counts as accepting the rules
the terms can be changed only by users
the company will ask again every month
qs.why: 계속 사용하면 약관에 동의한 것으로 간주한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Where can users change their privacy choices?
o: In the Settings menu
On the advertisers' websites
In an email to the company
On the page of each photo
qs.why: 설정의 개인정보 항목에서 바꿀 수 있어요.

items.title: Urgent: Verify Your Account
items.text:
Subject: Final Notice – Your Account Will Be Closed

Dear Customer,

We have detected unusual activity on your Starbank account. If you do not confirm your details within 24 hours, your account will be permanently suspended. Click the link below and enter your password, card number and date of birth to verify your identity immediately. Our security team has already blocked several payments from your account, and we cannot protect your money any longer without your help. This process takes only two minutes and requires no further action from you afterwards.

http://starbank-secure-login.example-help.net

Failure to respond will result in the loss of all funds. We apologise for any inconvenience this may cause.

Customer Support Team

qs.q: Which feature of the message is typical of a scam?
o: It is signed by a support team
It apologizes for the inconvenience
It has a subject line
It pressures the reader to act within a short time

qs.q: What is suspicious about the link?
o: It is much too long for a real bank to use as a web address

items.title: Review: Paper Moons
items.text: Paper Moons, the debut film from director Ines Calder, begins with a ten-minute shot of a girl walking home through a snowy town, and it is the most daring ten minutes I have seen this year. The camera barely moves, the sound is reduced to footsteps, and we learn who she is from what she looks at rather than what she says. Sadly, the film cannot keep up this confidence. Once the family drama begins, the dialogue turns stiff and a late twist feels borrowed from lesser movies. Still, the final image, a window lit against the dark, is so beautifully composed that I forgave much. It is flawed, but unforgettable.

qs.q: What is the reviewer's overall judgment of the film?
o: Perfect from beginning to end
Weak and not worth any attention
Impressive in places but uneven
Pleasant but forgettable

qs.q: How does the opening sequence tell us about the girl?

Through letters that she writes to her family every week
Through what she looks at, not through what she says
Through the loud music in the background

items.title: Teens and the News: A Ten-Year Change
items.text: A chart in this month's report compares where teenagers in one region get their news. In 2015, 46 percent named television first, 31 percent named websites and only 9 percent named social media. In 2025, social media leads with 52 percent, followed by video-sharing apps at 21 percent, while television has fallen to 8 percent. The report's author notes that the 2025 figures come from an online survey of 1,200 students, whereas the 2015 survey was carried out in classrooms with 3,000 students. She therefore warns against drawing sharp conclusions about the size of the change, though she says the direction is clear. The report also found that fewer than one in three teenagers could name the original source of the last story they read.

qs.q: What is the main finding of the report?
o: Teenagers trust television news more than they did ten years ago
Teenagers now rely mostly on social media, not television, for news
Teenagers no longer read any news at all
Teenagers prefer news websites to video-sharing apps
qs.why: 2025년에는 소셜 미디어가 1위(52%), 텔레비전은 8%로 줄었어요.

qs.q: Why does the author warn against drawing sharp conclusions?
o: The figures were copied from a rival report
The 2025 survey asked only about television
The students refused to answer honestly
The two surveys were carried out in different ways
qs.why: 조사 방식과 표본이 달라 변화의 크기를 단정하기 어려워요.

qs.q: What does the last sentence suggest about teenagers?
o: Many do not check where a story originally came from
Most can easily recall where they read their last news story

qs.why: 3분의 1 미만만 원출처를 댈 수 있다는 것은 출처를 잘 확인하지 않는다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Which statement about the data is accurate?

qs.why: 소셜 미디어는 9%에서 52%로 올랐어요.

items.title: Two Headlines, One Event
items.text: On Friday, a town's largest factory announced that it will cut 120 jobs while opening a new robotics unit employing 40 people. Two news sites reported the story differently. The Daily Courier ran the headline "Factory Slashes 120 Jobs in Brutal Blow to Town," with a photo of workers leaving through a gate. The Metro Business Wire chose "Factory Invests in Robotics, Creating 40 Skilled Roles." Both stories quoted the same company statement, and neither contained a false number. Yet a reader who saw only the headline would form a very different impression of the same facts. Media scholars call this "framing": the choice of which details to stress and which words to use. Comparing several reports is one way to see the frame around a story.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: One of the two news sites published false numbers
Factories should not use robots in towns
Photos are more reliable than headlines
Different headlines can shape how readers see the same facts
qs.why: 두 헤드라인의 비교로 프레이밍(틀 짓기)을 설명해요.

qs.q: The word "slashes" in the Courier's headline mainly
o: describes a tool used in the factory
sounds forceful and negative
gives exact information about wages
softens the news for readers
qs.why: slash는 강하고 부정적인 어감을 줘서 충격을 강조해요.

qs.q: What does the writer recommend to see a story's frame?
o: Reading several reports of the same event
Ignoring headlines altogether
Asking the factory to explain
Looking only at the photographs
qs.why: 여러 보도를 비교하라고 제안해요.

qs.q: Why does the passage mention the photo of workers leaving?

It proves that the factory has closed and that all the workers have left
It shows the robotics unit at work
It was added by the company statement
qs.why: 사진 선택도 감정을 더하는 프레이밍의 일부예요.

items.title: Advertising Rules for Influencers
items.text: Under new guidelines, influencers who are paid or given free products must make this clear to their followers. A brief tag such as "#ad" or "sponsored" has to appear where it can be seen at once, not hidden among twenty other hashtags or placed after the "more" button. In videos, the disclosure must be spoken or shown on screen, because many viewers watch without sound. Regulators say the rules exist because audiences tend to trust a recommendation from someone they follow more than they trust an advertisement. Companies that ignore the rules may be fined, and influencers may be held responsible alongside the brand. Some creators have welcomed the clarity, while others fear that open labels will make their posts look less sincere.

qs.q: What do the new guidelines require?
o: That influencers stop working with companies
That every video include music and subtitles
That paid promotion be clearly marked where followers can see it
That brands pay influencers a fixed amount
qs.why: 유료 홍보임을 눈에 띄는 곳에 분명히 표시해야 해요.

qs.q: Why must video disclosures be spoken or shown on screen?
o: Written tags cannot appear in videos
Many viewers watch without turning the sound on
Spoken words are easier to translate into other languages
Regulators prefer short videos
qs.why: 소리 없이 보는 시청자가 많기 때문이에요.

qs.q: According to regulators, why do the rules exist?
o: Advertisements are too expensive for most small companies to produce
Influencers earn more than they should

qs.why: 팔로우하는 사람의 추천을 광고보다 더 믿는 경향이 있기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What concern do some creators have?
o: Fines will be paid by their followers

qs.why: 공개 표시가 게시물을 덜 진정성 있게 보이게 할까 걱정해요.

qs.q: The phrase "held responsible alongside the brand" means that influencers

will take over the brand's business
are no longer responsible for posts
must choose a single brand to support
qs.why: 브랜드와 함께 책임을 질 수 있다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Storm Alert and Rumors
items.text: At 6:10 p.m., the regional weather service issued a storm alert for coastal areas, warning of winds up to 90 kilometers an hour after midnight. Within an hour, a message began spreading in group chats claiming that "all schools will be closed tomorrow and the bridge to the island has been shut by the army." Neither statement came from an official source. The school board said it would announce any closure by 6 a.m. through its website and text messages, and the highway department said the bridge would stay open unless winds became dangerous. Emergency officials urged residents to check official channels rather than forward unverified messages, noting that rumors during storms can lead people to make risky decisions, such as leaving home at the wrong time.

qs.q: What problem does the passage mainly describe?
o: A storm that damaged a school building
A bridge that was closed by mistake
A weather service that gave a false warning to coastal areas
Unconfirmed claims spreading during an emergency
qs.why: 공식 발표 외에 확인되지 않은 소문이 퍼지는 상황을 다뤄요.

qs.q: How will the school board inform families of any closure?
o: Through group chats organized by parents and students
Through a notice on the bridge
Through its website and text messages by 6 a.m.
Through the regional weather service
qs.why: 교육청은 오전 6시까지 웹사이트와 문자로 알리겠다고 했어요.

qs.q: Which statement about the bridge is supported by the passage?
o: It was closed by the army before midnight.
It was damaged by the earlier storm.
It would remain open unless the wind became dangerous.
It is used only by emergency vehicles.
qs.why: 도로 당국은 바람이 위험해지지 않는 한 열려 있을 것이라고 했어요.

qs.q: Why do officials warn against forwarding messages?
o: Messages cost too much to send
False information can lead to risky choices

qs.why: 소문이 위험한 결정을 부를 수 있기 때문이에요.

items.title: Streaming Now: Echoes of the Deep
items.text: Echoes of the Deep, a six-part documentary series, follows a team of marine biologists as they map a trench that no human has entered. Shot over three years, it combines footage from remote cameras with the researchers' own diaries, read aloud by actors. Critics have praised its patient pace and its refusal to turn every discovery into a drama; one called it "a lesson in how to look." Others find the narration too solemn and the music overly dramatic during scenes that need no help. The series ends with an honest admission that most of the trench is still unexplored. Suitable for ages twelve and above because of some tense scenes. All episodes are available with subtitles in nine languages.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of this text?
o: To give viewers information and opinions about a series
To teach marine biology to beginners
To sell cameras for deep-sea research
To announce that the deep trench has finally been given a name

qs.q: How does the series present the researchers' diaries?
o: They are shown as drawings
They are translated by the scientists
They are kept secret from viewers
They are read aloud by actors
qs.why: 연구자들의 일기를 배우들이 낭독한다고 나와요.

qs.q: What criticism do some viewers make?
o: The episodes are too short to follow

o: Much of the trench has not yet been studied

items.title: Why Your Feed Looks Like You
items.text: Open any social app and you will see posts chosen for you by an algorithm, a set of rules that predicts what you will click, like or share. Because the system learns from your past behavior, it tends to show more of what you already enjoy. This can be convenient: a fan of baking will never have to hunt for recipes. But researchers warn of a side effect sometimes called the "filter bubble," in which people see fewer views that differ from their own. Over time, this may make other opinions seem strange or unreasonable. Some platforms now offer a button to view posts in time order, though few users choose it. Experts suggest following a few accounts you disagree with, so that your feed does not always agree with you.

qs.q: What is the main topic of the passage?
o: How to become a famous baker online
Why social apps are losing users
How recommendation systems shape what we see and the risks
How to delete an account safely
qs.why: 알고리즘이 보여 주는 내용을 좌우하는 방식과 위험을 설명해요.

o: A tool that removes spam from posts

qs.q: Which advice do the experts give?

search

items.title: Letter to the Editor: Save Library Hours
items.text:
To the editor:

I was disappointed to learn that the Riverside Library will close at 5 p.m. on weekdays from next month. Your article described the decision as a "small adjustment," but for many families it is much more. Students like me rely on the library's quiet rooms and free internet after school, when our homes may be crowded or have no reliable connection. Cutting three evening hours may save the city some money, but it will cost young people a place to study. I urge the council to consider keeping the longer hours at least on two days a week, perhaps with volunteers. A library is not just a building for books; it is a service that treats every resident equally.

Yours sincerely,
Minseo Park

qs.q: Why did the writer send this letter?
o: To announce a new volunteer program
To persuade the council to reconsider shorter hours
To thank the newspaper for its article about the library
To complain about a noisy study room
qs.why: 도서관 단축 운영 결정을 재고해 달라고 설득하는 글이에요.

qs.q: What does the writer think of the phrase "small adjustment"?
o: It describes the change accurately
It was used by the council itself
It shows that the paper strongly supports the cuts
It understates the effect on families
qs.why: 가족들에게는 훨씬 큰 변화이므로 영향을 축소한 표현이라고 봐요.

qs.q: Which compromise does the writer suggest?
o: Longer hours on two weekdays, possibly run with volunteers

Charging a small fee for evening visits

qs.why: 일주일에 이틀은 연장 운영하되 자원봉사자를 활용하자고 제안해요.

qs.q: In the last sentence, "treats every resident equally" supports the idea that

qs.why: 모든 주민에게 동등한 서비스를 제공한다는 점을 들어 소득과 무관하게 도움이 된다는 주장을 뒷받침해요.

items.title: Public Service Announcement: Think Before You Share
items.text:
[Scene: A teenager sits on a bus, thumb hovering over her phone. A headline glows on the screen: "SHOCKING: Water Contains Dangerous Chemical!" The background music is fast and tense.]

Narrator: In ten seconds, you can reach a hundred friends. [The screen shows the post being shared; hearts and comments pour in.] Now, in ten more seconds, can you check whether it's true? [The music slows. The teenager opens a new tab and searches for the source. A calm green check appears beside a government health page.] The headline was false. [She deletes the draft.] Before you share, stop, search, and confirm.

[Closing text on screen: "Be the one who stops the rumor."]

qs.q: What does the change in the music suggest?

The video is nearly over
The teenager has just received a phone call from a friend

qs.q: What is the purpose of the green check mark?

It signals that the source is reliable
It warns that the page is unsafe

items.title: Cutting Your First Video
items.text: Beginners often believe that a good video depends on expensive equipment, but editing matters far more. Start by watching all your footage and writing down the best moments; most clips contain only a few seconds worth keeping. Next, arrange these moments so that each shot leads naturally to the following one. Cut on action, for example when a person opens a door, since our eyes hardly notice a change at that moment. Keep the audio clear: viewers forgive shaky images much sooner than muffled speech. Finally, add music at a low volume and check the video on a phone as well as a computer. If you can explain the story of your video in one sentence, the edit is probably focused enough.

qs.q: What is the writer's main message?
o: Careful editing improves a video more than costly equipment does
Phones are better than professional cameras
Music is the most important part of a video
Beginners should avoid editing their own footage at the start
qs.why: 장비보다 편집이 더 중요하다는 것이 핵심이에요.

qs.q: Why does the writer suggest cutting on action?
o: The footage becomes shorter in total
The sound is easier to record
The change is less noticeable to viewers
The actor can rest between shots
qs.why: 동작 중에 자르면 시청자 눈이 장면 전환을 거의 알아채지 못해요.

qs.q: According to the passage, which is more easily forgiven by viewers?
o: Unclear speech
Shaky pictures
Very quiet music
Too many short clips
qs.why: 흔들리는 영상은 불분명한 음성보다 더 쉽게 용서된다고 해요.

items.title: Interview: A Reporter on Slow News
items.text: When asked why she left a fast-paced online newsroom, reporter Sora Lindgren answers without hesitation. "We were rewarded for speed, not accuracy," she says. "A story was judged by how many people clicked it in the first ten minutes." Now she writes one long article a month for a small magazine. Each piece takes weeks of research, and every statistic is checked by a second person. Lindgren admits that her readers are fewer and that the pay is lower. Nevertheless, she believes that a smaller audience that trusts you is worth more than a huge audience that forgets you. "People think slow means boring," she says with a smile. "I think slow means someone actually checked."

o: She felt that speed counted for more than accuracy
She wanted a job with higher pay
She was dismissed after making a serious factual mistake
She disliked writing long articles

qs.q: How is each article at her new magazine checked?
o: The readers vote on the topic

qs.q: What does Lindgren admit about her new job?
o: The articles are shorter than before
The work is faster than at the newsroom
The audience is smaller and the pay is lower

items.title: Using Pictures Without Getting Into Trouble
items.text: Many students believe that any image found online is free to use. In fact, most pictures are protected by copyright, which means that the creator decides how they may be used. Using a photo in a private school assignment is often allowed, but posting it on a public website may require permission. Some creators share their work under licenses that let others use it if they give credit; websites for such images usually show the terms on each page. Always note the creator's name, the source and the license. If you are not sure, choose an image you have taken yourself. This habit not only protects you from legal problems, but also shows respect for the person who made the picture.

o: All pictures on the internet are free to copy

Students should never use online photographs in any of their schoolwork

qs.why: 대부분의 이미지에는 저작권이 있으므로 사용 조건을 확인해야 해요.

qs.q: According to the passage, when might permission be needed?
o: When a photo is posted on a public website
When a photo is used in private homework
When you take a picture yourself
When you credit the creator
qs.why: 공개 웹사이트에 올릴 때는 허락이 필요할 수 있다고 해요.

qs.q: What does a license that requires credit allow?
o: Selling the work as your own
Changing the creator's name
Using the work with no conditions at all
Using the work if you name the creator
qs.why: 출처(창작자)를 밝히면 사용할 수 있게 하는 라이선스예요.

qs.q: What is the safest choice when you are unsure?
o: Choose the most popular picture
Remove the creator's name
Ask a friend to post it for you
Use a picture you made yourself
qs.why: 직접 찍은 이미지를 쓰라고 권해요.

qs.q: What additional benefit of crediting does the writer mention?
o: It shows respect to the creator
It makes the picture look better
It lets you earn money
It shortens the assignment
qs.why: 출처를 적는 것은 제작자에 대한 존중을 보여 줘요.

items.title: Petition: Keep Our Newsroom Open
items.text: The Greenfield Gazette, which has reported on our town for 94 years, plans to close its newsroom and rely on stories from a distant head office. We, the undersigned, ask the owners to reconsider. Without local reporters, who will attend council meetings, question officials or tell us why the river keeps flooding? National outlets rarely cover the small decisions that shape our daily lives. Studies suggest that when local papers disappear, fewer people vote in local elections and public spending tends to rise, because fewer people watch how money is used. We do not ask for the paper to stay the same. We ask for a future in which our community still has someone whose job is to ask questions on its behalf. Please add your name.

qs.q: What do the petitioners want?
o: The town to publish its own newspaper
The owners to keep a local newsroom in operation
The council to stop holding meetings
Readers to pay higher subscription fees to the owners
qs.why: 지역 편집국을 닫지 말아 달라는 청원이에요.

qs.q: How do the writers support their argument?
o: By listing the salaries of the reporters
By criticizing the head office personally
By pointing to what local reporting does for the community
By describing the history of printing
qs.why: 지역 보도가 공동체에 하는 역할을 근거로 들어요.

qs.q: The sentence "we do not ask for the paper to stay the same" shows that the writers
o: want the paper to stop printing soon
dislike the current stories
are open to changes in the paper
expect the paper to grow larger
qs.why: 신문이 그대로 유지되기를 요구하는 것은 아니며 변화에 열려 있다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Which claim is made as a result of studies?
o: Spending tends to rise when fewer people watch it
Rivers flood more often without newspapers
National outlets cover local issues better than local papers
People vote more when papers are online
qs.why: 지역 신문이 사라지면 공공 지출이 늘어나는 경향이 있다고 해요.

items.title: Does Coffee Help You Live Longer?
items.text: A headline this week declared, "Coffee Drinkers Live Longer, Study Finds." The research, published in a health journal, followed 40,000 adults for twelve years and found that those who drank two to three cups a day were less likely to die during the study than non-drinkers. However, the study was observational: it did not assign people to drink or avoid coffee, so it cannot show that coffee itself was responsible. Coffee drinkers in the group also tended to exercise more and smoke less. The authors themselves wrote that their results "suggest an association" and should not be read as advice. Still, the headline was shared widely, while the careful wording of the study was left out of most reports.

qs.q: Why is the headline considered misleading?
o: It describes a study that was never carried out
It exaggerates the number of people studied
It mentions the wrong journal
It treats a link in the data as if it were proven cause
qs.why: 관찰 연구는 상관관계만 보여 주는데 헤드라인은 원인인 것처럼 말해요.

qs.q: What does it mean that the study was "observational"?
o: The researchers measured the caffeine in each cup in a laboratory test
The researchers watched what people did without assigning behavior
The researchers asked people to avoid coffee
The researchers tested animals first
qs.why: 참가자에게 행동을 지정하지 않고 관찰만 했다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why does the passage mention exercise and smoking?
o: They show that coffee makes people exercise
They may explain the difference between the two groups
They prove that smoking is harmless
They describe the daily routines of the authors of the study
qs.why: 다른 요인들이 결과 차이를 설명할 수 있기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What does the final sentence criticize?
o: The authors' choice of journal
The number of adults in the study
The length of the research
The media's loss of the study's careful wording
qs.why: 기사들이 연구의 신중한 표현을 빼 버렸다는 점을 비판해요.

qs.q: The word "association" is closest in meaning to
o: connection
agreement
organization
competition
qs.why: association은 '연관성'이라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Sunrise Cereal: Packaging Claims
items.text: The front of the Sunrise Oats box shows a smiling child, a golden field and the words "Natural Energy For Active Kids." A green banner says "Made With Whole Grains," and a bold circle reads "25% Less Sugar!" On the back, smaller print explains that the sugar comparison is with the company's own earlier recipe, not with other brands, and that whole grains make up just 14 percent of the ingredients. The nutrition panel shows 11 grams of sugar per serving, and sugar is the second item in the ingredient list. A consumer group has argued that such claims do not break any rule, yet they lead shoppers to assume that the product is healthier than it is.

qs.q: What does the "25% Less Sugar!" claim actually compare?
o: The cereal with all of the other cereals on the market
The cereal with fresh fruit
The new recipe with the company's earlier recipe
The amount of sugar in one box and in one bowl
qs.why: 뒷면 작은 글씨에 자사의 이전 제품과 비교한 것이라고 나와요.

qs.q: What is the main point made about the packaging?
o: It breaks the rules on food labeling
It contains no information about sugar
It is aimed at adults who count calories
Its prominent claims can suggest more than the facts support
qs.why: 규정 위반은 아니지만 소비자가 실제보다 건강하다고 생각하게 만든다는 지적이에요.

qs.q: Which feature is a visual cue meant to attract families?
o: The nutrition panel
The smiling child and golden field
The ingredient list
The small print on the back of the box
qs.why: 웃는 아이와 황금빛 들판은 시각적 연출이에요.

qs.q: Which detail most clearly weakens the "Made With Whole Grains" banner?
o: The banner is green
The box shows a child
Whole grains are only 14 percent of the contents
The cereal is sold in a large box with a green banner
qs.why: 통곡물이 14%에 불과하다는 점이 문구의 인상을 약화시켜요.

items.title: Planning the School News Video
items.text:
Yuna: Our school news video needs a topic. Any ideas?
Marcus: What about the new recycling program? Everyone has seen the colored bins, but nobody knows how they work.
Yuna: Good idea. But a video made only of talking is boring. How can we show the process?
Marcus: We could film the bins being emptied, then follow the bags to the sorting center. Close-ups of the machines would be dramatic.
Yuna: True, but we must get permission before filming anyone. And let's interview the cleaning staff. They know more than anybody.
Marcus: Agreed. Should we add background music?
Yuna: Only softly. If it's too loud, viewers won't hear the interviews.
Marcus: Okay. And we'll add captions, so people can watch in the hallway without sound.
Yuna: Perfect. Let's write the script tonight and film on Thursday.

qs.q: What is the main topic of the conversation?
o: Deciding how to make an interesting video about recycling
Choosing a new school recycling program
Arguing about who should star in the video
Repairing the school's video equipment
qs.why: 재활용 프로그램에 대한 영상을 어떻게 흥미롭게 만들지 논의해요.

qs.q: Why does Yuna want to avoid a video made only of talking?
o: She thinks it would be dull
She believes talking is not allowed
She dislikes the cleaning staff
She wants the video to be shorter
qs.why: 말만 나오는 영상은 지루하다고 해요.

qs.q: Why will the students add captions?
o: The interviews are in a foreign language
The cleaning staff speak too quietly
Viewers may watch without sound in a hallway
The school requires captions on all student videos
qs.why: 복도에서 소리 없이 볼 수 있기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What does Yuna say about background music?
o: It should be loud and dramatic
It should be quiet enough for the interviews to be heard
It is unnecessary for any school video
It should be chosen by the cleaning staff before the filming
qs.why: 음악이 크면 인터뷰가 들리지 않는다고 해요.

qs.q: What must the students do before filming people?
o: Pay them a small fee
Write them a formal invitation
Practice the interview questions
Get permission from them
qs.why: 사람을 촬영하기 전에 허락을 받아야 한다고 해요.

items.title: Checking the Source
items.text:
Ms. Reyes: Jisoo, your presentation says that teenagers sleep only four hours on average. Where did you find that?
Jisoo: In a post with a colorful chart. It had thousands of shares.
Ms. Reyes: Popularity isn't evidence. Who made the chart?
Jisoo: Um, I didn't see a name. It just said "Health Facts Daily."
Ms. Reyes: And did it mention how the data was collected?
Jisoo: No. But the numbers looked official.
Ms. Reyes: That's the trick. A professional design can make weak information appear strong. Try searching for the figure along with the word "survey."
Jisoo: I found a study from a national health agency. It says the average is just under eight hours for fourteen-year-olds.
Ms. Reyes: So the chart was wrong by half. What will you change?
Jisoo: I'll use the study, and add the date and the link to my slides.

qs.q: Why does Ms. Reyes question Jisoo's chart?
o: The colors of the chart are too bright
Its creator and method of collecting data are not identified
The chart is too large for the slide
The chart was not shared enough times
qs.why: 제작자와 자료 수집 방법이 밝혀지지 않았어요.

qs.q: What does Ms. Reyes mean by "That's the trick"?
o: Professional-looking design can hide weak evidence
Charts are always unreliable
Teachers like to test students with tricky questions
Searching online is difficult
qs.why: 전문적인 디자인이 부실한 정보를 강해 보이게 만든다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What did Jisoo find after searching again?
o: A second chart that supports the figure of four hours
A video by a popular creator
A message from the chart's author
A study giving a much higher average for sleep
qs.why: 전국 보건 기관 연구에서 평균이 8시간 가까이였어요.

qs.q: What will Jisoo add to her slides?
o: A second colorful chart
Her teacher's opinion
The date and the link of the study
The number of times the post was shared
qs.why: 날짜와 링크를 추가하겠다고 해요.

items.title: The Ad That Seemed Too Good
items.text:
Hana: Did you see that ad for Glowfast? "Clear skin in three days or your money back!"
Tomás: I did. A lot of people in the comments say it worked.
Hana: Have you noticed that the comments are all very similar? "Amazing!" "Changed my life!" They sound like they were written by the same person.
Tomás: Maybe. But the before-and-after photos are impressive.
Hana: The two photos have different lighting, though. In the "after" picture, she's also wearing makeup.
Tomás: Hm, I hadn't noticed. What about the money-back promise?
Hana: I clicked the link. You have to return the unopened bottle within twenty-four hours, which is impossible if you want to test it for three days.
Tomás: Oh. So it only looks like a guarantee.
Hana: Exactly. I'd rather ask a pharmacist.

qs.q: Why does Hana doubt the comments?
o: They are written in different languages
They are much too long
They are similar and seem to have a single author
They criticize the product too strongly
qs.why: 비슷한 댓글들이 한 사람이 쓴 것처럼 보여요.

qs.q: What problem does Hana notice with the before-and-after photos?
o: The photos are too small to see
The conditions in the two pictures are not the same
The pictures seem to show two completely different people
The photos were taken years apart
qs.why: 조명이 다르고 '이후' 사진에서는 화장도 했어요.

qs.q: What is wrong with the money-back promise?
o: The return deadline is shorter than the testing period
The product costs more than advertised
The company is located abroad
The bottle must be completely empty before it is returned
qs.why: 3일 사용 후 효과를 보려면 24시간 내 반품이 불가능해요.

qs.q: What will Hana most likely do about her skin problem?
o: Buy the product to test it
Post a comment praising the ad
Wait for another advertisement
Seek advice from a professional
qs.why: 약사에게 묻겠다고 해요.

qs.q: Tomás's final comment, "it only looks like a guarantee," means that the offer
o: is sure to work
is hidden from buyers
is available only in some local stores
seems safe but is not in practice
qs.why: 겉보기엔 보증이지만 실제로는 그렇지 않다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Fixing a Mistake in the Story
items.text:
Editor: Joon, a reader wrote that your article on the bus strike has the wrong date. You wrote the 12th, but the strike began on the 21st.
Joon: Really? I'll check my notes. Oh no, I swapped the digits. I'm sorry.
Editor: It happens. The important thing is how we respond. Have you fixed the online version?
Joon: Yes, I just did. Should I delete the old sentence quietly?
Editor: No. We add a line at the bottom saying what was changed and when. Otherwise readers who saw the first version may wonder.
Joon: That makes sense. What about the newsletter that went out this morning?
Editor: We'll include a short correction in tomorrow's edition. And next time, ask a colleague to read the dates and numbers aloud before publication.
Joon: I will. Thank you for explaining it calmly.

qs.q: What mistake did Joon make?
o: He wrote a wrong date by switching digits
He misspelled the name of a union leader
He quoted a source who did not exist
He attached the wrong photo to the article
qs.why: 12일과 21일의 숫자를 바꿔 썼어요.

qs.q: Why does the editor tell Joon not to delete the old sentence quietly?
o: The old sentence was accurate
Readers of the first version deserve to know about the change
The website cannot be edited twice
The strike dates were not important
qs.why: 처음 버전을 본 독자를 위해 수정 사실을 밝혀야 해요.

qs.q: How will the mistake be handled in the newsletter?
o: The newsletter will be recalled
Joon will resign from his post
A short correction will appear in the next edition
Subscribers will be sent a refund for the newsletter
qs.why: 내일 호에 짧은 정정문을 싣겠다고 해요.

qs.q: What does the editor advise for the future?
o: Avoid writing about strikes
Use fewer numbers in articles
Ask a colleague to read dates and numbers aloud first
Publish stories before checking
qs.why: 동료가 날짜와 숫자를 소리 내어 읽어 주게 하라고 해요.

items.q: Which headline is the clearest example of clickbait?
o: You Won't Believe What This Teacher Did Next
City Library to Extend Weekend Opening Hours
Study Links Sleep Habits to Test Scores
Mayor Announces Plan to Repair Three Bridges
items.why: 독자의 호기심만 자극하고 정보를 숨기는 제목이 클릭 유도형이에요.

items.q: You need reliable statistics on unemployment in your country. Which source is best?
o: A post by a popular influencer
A discussion thread on a hobby forum
An advertisement for a popular job-search app
A report from the national statistics office
items.why: 공식 통계 기관의 보고서가 가장 신뢰할 만한 1차 자료예요.

items.q: A news site labels an article "Sponsored Content." What does this mean?
o: The article was written by the site's top reporter
A company paid for the article to be published
The article has been checked by a government office
The article has been removed for a mistake
items.why: sponsored content는 광고주가 비용을 낸 콘텐츠를 뜻해요.

items.q: Which search query is best for finding pages that contain the exact phrase "climate change policy"?
o: climate change OR policy
"climate change policy"
climate OR change OR policy
policy NOT climate change
items.why: 따옴표로 묶으면 그 구절이 그대로 들어간 결과를 찾아요.

items.q: You want results only from government sites ending in ".gov" about "school lunch." Which query is best?
o: school lunch .gov-only
gov:school lunch
school lunch @.gov
school lunch site:.gov
items.why: site: 연산자로 특정 도메인의 결과만 검색할 수 있어요.

items.q: Which sentence reports the event in the most neutral way?
o: The council voted to raise parking fees by 10 percent.
The council greedily pushed through a very hated fee hike.
Drivers were hit with yet another outrageous fee.
The council shamelessly punished drivers again.
items.why: 감정이 담긴 단어(greedily, hated 등) 없이 사실만 전달하는 문장이 중립적이에요.

items.q: Which statement is an opinion rather than a fact?
o: The park opened in May.
The park has two playgrounds.
The new park is the most beautiful place in town.
The park covers four hectares.
items.why: '가장 아름답다'는 주관적 평가라서 의견이에요.

items.q: Why does a social media user add #FloodRelief to a post?
o: So the post will be deleted by the app after a day
So the writer's name is hidden
So the photo is automatically edited
So people searching that topic can find the post
items.why: 해시태그는 주제별 검색과 분류를 돕는 장치예요.

items.q: What is the main purpose of alt text added to an online image?
o: To make the image load more slowly
To describe the image for people who cannot see it
To protect the image from copying
To place an advertisement over the middle of the image
items.why: 대체 텍스트는 시각 장애인이나 이미지가 보이지 않을 때 내용을 알려 줘요.

items.q: A photo shared online claims to show today's protest. What is the best tool to check whether it is old?
o: A spelling checker
A video editor
A reverse image search
A password manager
items.why: 역이미지 검색으로 같은 사진이 과거에 쓰였는지 확인할 수 있어요.

items.q: Which set of keywords best captures this sentence? "A new app lets farmers predict heavy rain three days ahead."
o: app, farmers, predict, rain
new, lets, ahead, days
heavy, three, a, the
farmers, lets, new, three, ahead
items.why: 핵심어는 내용을 담은 명사·동사 위주로 고르는 것이 좋아요.

items.q: Which sentence is the best one-sentence summary of this text? "A town replaced its paper bus tickets with phone passes. Costs fell by a third, but older residents complained that the change was hard to learn, so the town now offers free lessons."
o: A town cut costs with phone passes and began helping older users.
A town printed new paper bus tickets for older residents.
A town ended its bus service after residents complained.
A town spent a third of its money on free phone lessons.
items.why: 요약은 핵심(비용 절감과 노년층 지원)을 담아야 해요.

items.q: An editor wants to suggest changes to a shared article without erasing the writer's words. Which tool should she use?
o: Print preview
Screen capture
Track changes
Auto-play
items.why: 변경 내용 추적 기능은 원문을 지우지 않고 수정 제안을 보여 줘요.

items.q: Which web address is most likely to belong to a phishing site pretending to be Northbank?
o: www.northbank.com
northbank.secure-login-check.com
www.northbank.com/help/contact-us
support.northbank.com
items.why: 공식 도메인 앞뒤에 다른 말을 붙인 주소는 가짜 사이트일 가능성이 커요.

items.q: You post a photo of your concert ticket. What should you do first to protect your information?
o: Add your home address as a caption
Tag the ticket seller's account
Post it again with a different photo filter
Cover the barcode and personal details
items.why: 바코드와 개인 정보를 가리는 것이 정보 보안의 기본이에요.

items.q: A report says a company is "downsizing." What does the word most likely mean?
o: Moving to a smaller office building
Reducing the number of workers
Lowering the price of its goods
Making its products smaller in size
items.why: downsizing은 인력을 줄인다는 완곡한 표현이에요.

items.q: In the sentence "The missing funds may be only the tip of the iceberg," what does the idiom suggest?
o: A larger problem probably lies hidden
The problem will soon disappear
The cause of the problem is cold weather
The funds will be found in the north
items.why: 빙산의 일각은 더 큰 문제가 숨어 있을 수 있음을 뜻해요.

items.q: If a video "goes viral," what happens to it?
o: It is removed because of a virus
It is shown only to the creator's family
It is translated into another language
It is shared rapidly by very many people
items.why: go viral은 빠르게 널리 퍼진다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: What does the headline "Mayor to Open New Library" tell us about time?
o: The event happened last year
The event is happening right now
The event is planned for the future
The event was cancelled
items.why: 헤드라인에서 'to + 동사원형'은 예정된 일을 나타내요.

items.q: Which sentence puts the focus on the people who were helped, not on who helped them?
o: Rescuers saved two hikers from the mountain last night.
The mountain rescue team saved two hikers.
Two hikers were rescued from the mountain last night.
Last night a rescue team rescued two hikers.
items.why: 수동태는 행위자보다 도움을 받은 대상에 초점을 둬요.

items.q: Which phrase in an ad mainly creates a feeling of urgency?
o: Made from natural ingredients only
Offer ends at midnight tonight!
Loved by customers everywhere
Designed in our local studio
items.why: 마감 시간을 강조하는 표현이 긴박감을 만들어요.

items.q: A campaign says, "Everyone who tried our tea felt better, so tea cures colds." Which weakness does this reasoning show?
o: It assumes the tea caused the improvement
It uses too many technical words for readers
It is written in a formal style
It mentions a type of drink
items.why: 먼저 일어난 일이 원인이라고 가정하는 오류예요.

items.q: A news story says, "According to an official who asked not to be named, the plan will change." What does this do to the story's credibility?
o: It proves that the claim is correct
It shows the plan has already changed
It means the official lied to the reporter
It makes the claim harder for readers to verify
items.why: 익명 취재원은 독자가 확인하기 어렵게 만들어요.

items.q: A report states: "Sales rose 30 percent in March," but does not mention that they fell 40 percent in the previous two months. What is this technique called?
o: Cross-referencing
Quoting
Translating
Cherry-picking
items.why: 유리한 자료만 골라 보여 주는 것을 체리피킹이라고 해요.

items.q: What is a "paywall" on a news website?
o: A barrier that requires payment to read more
A warning about harmful content
A list of the most-read stories
A filter that blocks advertisements from the page
items.why: 유료 구독을 해야 기사를 볼 수 있게 하는 장벽이에요.

items.q: A website publishes invented stories written like real news in order to make readers laugh. This kind of writing is called
o: a press release
satire
a correction
a documentary
items.why: 풍자(satire)는 웃음과 비판을 위해 꾸며 낸 이야기예요.

items.q: Which description best fits an "echo chamber" online?
o: A chat room that repeats every message twice
A website that records people's voices
A group where members hear only opinions that match their own
A video with a loud sound effect
items.why: 비슷한 의견만 반복해서 듣는 집단을 에코 챔버라고 해요.

items.q: In a news video about a disaster, slow, quiet piano music is played under the images. What effect does it most likely have?
o: It makes the report seem funny
It warns viewers to leave their homes
